data.title: Will Anthropic pull off a November IPO? Time is running out to file key paperwork.
data.description:
By William Gavin

If market pressures keep building, Anthropic 'could reasonably decide it is better to stay private and wait for a better opportunity,' one portfolio manager says

Anthropic, which makes the Claude suite of products, is one of the pillars of the AI boom.

Anthropic may be just days away from making a major step toward becoming a public company - but there's still time for things to change.

The company is one of the biggest pillars of the artificial-intelligence industry, and its anticipated initial public offering is likely to reinforce that. Anthropic is reportedly seeking a valuation of as much as $2 trillion, which could result in an even more explosive IPO than SpaceX's (SPCX) $1.77 trillion debut earlier this year.

According a Reuters report on Thursday, the Claude chatbot maker plans to hold its IPO in the middle of November, which means time is running out to file some important paperwork. The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission requires a company to publicly file its prospectus at least 15 days before it launches a roadshow.

Jay Ritter, who leads the University of Florida's IPO Initiative, told MarketWatch that Anthropic has some time if it still wants to go public before Thanksgiving. If the company were to hold its IPO as late as Nov. 24 and start its roadshow with investors on Nov. 16, Anthropic would have until late next week to publicly file its S-1 document, he said.

However, it's also possible that Anthropic decides to push back its IPO. The company was once expected to publicly unveil its IPO prospectus shortly after Labor Day, which could have set the stage for it to list later in September. Experts say it's likely, but not certain, that Anthropic will still want to make a debut now.

Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The market has become less hospitable to AI companies lately, which is one factor that could give pause to Anthropic's management team. Joe Tigay, a portfolio manager at the Rational Equity Armor Fund HDCAX, told MarketWatch that persistent inflation and high energy prices could also be cause for concern.

"Historically, that combination of slowing growth and persistent inflation can be where stock markets crack. If those pressures keep building, Anthropic could reasonably decide it is better to stay private and wait for a better opportunity," Tigay told MarketWatch over email.

But the market needs a successful Anthropic IPO to prove that AI has staying power, argued Jim Lebenthal, chief market strategist at Cerity Partners. He noted that the longevity and economics of the AI industry have been further called into question recently.

Shares of the neocloud company CoreWeave (CRWV), for example, have dropped roughly 30% over the last two weeks on concerns about the company's ability to manage its debt. Even companies that are swimming in cash have been swept up in the downward action. Micron Technology's stock (MU) has lost 17% over the past month against the broader backdrop of fears over AI spending and financing.

"It's reasonable to have questions. It's reasonable even to have doubts," Lebenthal said. "But the health of the overall equity market and the health of the U.S. economy relies vitally on the artificial-intelligence industry being successful."

Of course, Anthropic's reasons for going public wouldn't be to buoy stock-market sentiment toward AI. Simply put, Anthropic needs the cash, according to Andrew Rocco, a stock strategist at Zacks Investment Research.

The biggest AI companies have shown that "they're basically willing to spend as much as they can in order to capture more customers and try and be the dominant AI player," Rocco told MarketWatch. "In my view they're going to try and get this out because they do need that capital, especially since it's going to be probably harder to just raise it in the private market."

Anthropic could spend as much as $750 billion on AI compute capacity in the coming years, according to the Wall Street Journal, which cited a copy of its draft IPO prospectus. The Journal also noted that Anthropic recorded a net loss of more than $80 billion in the first half of 2026 against revenue of $16.3 billion, though the loss was largely driven by accounting adjustments rather than fundamental business developments.

Rocco noted that prediction markets show an 80% chance of the company going public by the end of the year.

-William Gavin

data.title: Copper One Commences Up to 10,000 Foot Phase 2 Drill Program at Flagship Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold Project, Nevada
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

Vancouver, BC – October 23, 2026 – TheNewswire - Copper One Resources Corp. ("Copper One") (CSE: CEXY | OTCID: CEXYF | FSE: IW8 | WKN: A42AGR) (the "Company") is pleased to announce that diamond core drilling has commenced at its 100%-owned flagship Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold Project (“Majuba Hill” or the “Project”) in Pershing County, Nevada.

The Company’s expanded Phase 2 diamond core drilling program (the “Phase 2 Program”) comprises up to 10,000 feet (3,048 metres) of HQ/PQ diamond core drilling. The Phase 2 Program is intended to accelerate systematic testing of priority targets at Majuba Hill and support the Company’s objective of advancing the Project toward a maiden mineral resource estimate prepared in accordance with National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects (“NI 43-101”). More than 90,000 feet (27,432 metres) have been drilled to date at Majuba Hill across more than 100 drill holes.

Assay results from the completed 2026 Phase 1 drill program remain pending and will be announced once received, reviewed and validated.

David Greenway, President and Chief Executive Officer of Copper One, stated: “With Phase 2 drilling now underway at Majuba Hill, we are advancing the systematic testing of priority targets through an expanded program of up to 10,000 feet. While assay results from Phase 1 remain pending, the geological information collected is helping guide our ongoing exploration. Evolve’s personnel, equipment and operational experience, supported by its EVX Connect platform, provide our technical team with timely drilling data and core photographs to support informed decisions as the program advances. We look forward to reporting Phase 1 assay results once received, reviewed and validated, alongside further updates from Phase 2 drilling.”

Click Image To View Full Size

Figure 1: Chalcopyrite and pyrrhotite observed within the breccia zone in hole MHB-37B at approximately 1,982 feet (604 metres). Assays are pending. Visual identification is preliminary and should not be considered a substitute for laboratory assay results.

Source: CME Group, Copper Futures Overview, last updated September 18, 2026, at 4:49 a.m. CT. Market data is delayed by at least 10 minutes.

Phase 2 Program Highlights

  • Expanded program of up to 10,000 feet (3,048 metres) of diamond core drilling.


  • Initial approximately 5,000 feet (1,524 metres) contracted to Evolve using one portable HQ/PQ core drill.


  • Continuous, two-shift drilling operations planned on a 24-hour-per-day, seven-day-per-week basis.


  • Maximum planned hole depth under the initial scope of approximately 1,700 feet (518 metres), with final collar locations, azimuths, inclinations and depths to be determined by the Company’s technical team.


  • Real-time operational visibility through Evolve’s EVX Connect platform.


Click Image To View Full Size

Figure 2: Elevated view of drill pad 26DPH-8 at Copper One Resources Corp.’s 100%-owned Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold Project in Pershing County, Nevada.

Real-Time Drill Program Technology

As previously announced the Company engaged Evolve Exploration Nevada, LLC (“Evolve”) to undertake the Phase 2 diamond core drilling.

Every Evolve drill rig operates on EVX Connect, Evolve’s real-time operational platform. Through EVX Connect, Copper One expects to receive live drilling metrics, digital PLOD reporting, drill-hole coordinate tracking, streamlined invoicing and high-quality photographs of drill core as it is recovered. Information will be accessible through web and mobile interfaces, providing the Company’s technical and management teams with timely visibility into drilling progress and field operations.

About the Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold Project, Nevada

Majuba Hill is Copper One Resources Corp.’s flagship copper-silver-gold exploration project, located in Pershing County, Nevada, USA. Nevada ranked first globally on the Investment Attractiveness Index in the Fraser Institute’s Annual Survey of Mining Companies 2025. The property comprises approximately 9,684 acres (3,919 hectares) and is situated approximately 70 miles (113 road kilometres) southwest of Winnemucca and 156 miles (251 kilometres) northeast of Reno.

The project benefits from excellent infrastructure, including year-round road access, nearby electrical power, water, and access to a skilled mining workforce. Majuba Hill is a past-producing copper mine with an extensive exploration database, including approximately 89,395 feet (27,248 metres) of historical drilling, providing a strong technical foundation for ongoing exploration aimed at further defining the extent and economic potential of the mineralized system.

Exploration has outlined a large copper-silver-gold hydrothermal mineralized system that remains open for expansion. Current exploration is focused on advancing the Company's geological model through systematic drilling, geological mapping, geochemical sampling, and structural interpretation to evaluate the scale, continuity, and significance of mineralization. Additional drilling and technical studies will be required to further define the extent and economic potential of the mineralized system.

Click Image To View Full Size

Figure 3: Majuba Hill 2026 drilling target zones, completed drill holes and planned drill holes.

Qualified Person

The scientific and technical information contained in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Larry Segerstrom, M.Sc. (Geology), CPG, a non-independent consulting geologist to the Company and a Qualified Person as defined by National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects.

About Copper One Resources Corp.

Copper One Resources Corp. is focused on identifying, acquiring and advancing high-potential copper, copper-silver-gold and copper-molybdenum projects to help meet global demand for critical metals used in electrification, AI infrastructure and data centres, renewable energy, defence and power-system modernization.

The Company's flagship asset is the Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold District, located approximately 156 miles (251 kilometres) from Reno, Nevada. Majuba Hill is an exploration-stage porphyry copper project situated in an established mining jurisdiction with existing infrastructure, where ongoing exploration is focused on evaluating the scale and continuity of a copper-silver-gold mineralized system.

Copper One also owns a 100% interest in the Redonda Copper-Molybdenum Project, located northeast of Campbell River in British Columbia's Vancouver Mining Division. The district-scale project comprises approximately 2,746.46 hectares (6,786 acres) across nine mineral claims and hosts a porphyry-style copper-molybdenum system within the Coast Suture Zone, a geological belt known for porphyry copper and skarn mineralization. Systematic exploration is continuing to evaluate the scale and continuity of the mineralized system.

In addition, Copper One holds an option to earn up to a 100% interest in the Redhill Property, located south of Ashcroft, British Columbia, adjacent to the Trans-Canada Highway. The 4,736-hectare (11,704-acre) property hosts volcanogenic massive sulphide (VMS) mineralization prospective for copper, zinc, silver and gold, while also demonstrating potential for epithermal gold mineralization.

Copper One also owns a 100% interest in the Sport Project in Utah through its wholly owned subsidiary, Rooinek Mining Corp., expanding the Company’s portfolio of North American copper exploration assets.

Copper One is advancing its portfolio through systematic exploration, modern geological modelling and disciplined technical evaluation. The Company remains committed to responsible exploration practices, technical transparency and the disciplined advancement of critical-metals projects across North America.

data.title: Uranium One Mining Corp. Engages Adrian Huerta Ruiz as Technical Advisor for Athabasca Basin Uranium Exploration
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

    Vancouver, BC – October 23, 2026 - TheNewswire – Uranium One  Mining Corp. ("Uranium One" or the "Company") (UUU: CSE | UUUFF: OTCID | SL51: Frankfurt) is pleased to announce that it has engaged Adrian Huerta Ruiz as a Technical Advisor focused on the Company’s uranium exploration interests in Saskatchewan’s Athabasca Basin.

    About Huerta Ruiz, CPG

    Mr. Huerta Ruiz is an experienced exploration geologist and Certified Professional Geologist (CPG) with the American Institute of Professional Geologists (AIPG), bringing more than 14 years of technical and operational experience in mineral exploration and mining.

    Based in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, Mr. Huerta Ruiz has direct experience working on uranium exploration projects in the Athabasca Basin, including geological core logging and sampling of sandstone- and basement-hosted uranium systems. His expertise encompasses exploration program management, drill planning, geological mapping, geological interpretation, and quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) procedures.

    In his role as Technical Advisor to Uranium One Mining Corp., Mr. Huerta Ruiz is expected to provide technical guidance and support the evaluation, planning and prioritization of exploration activities across the Company's Athabasca Basin uranium portfolio, including preparations for its upcoming field exploration season.

    “We are pleased to have Adrian joining the Uranium One team,” said Larry Segerstrom, Director and P.Geo. “His experience adds to our technical strength as the Company prepares for its maiden exploration season in the Athabasca Basin. We look forward to his input as we evaluate our properties and set priorities for fieldwork.”

    Uranium One’s Athabasca Basin Portfolio

    The Company’s portfolio comprises three highly prospective uranium projects in Saskatchewan’s Athabasca Basin, which is widely recognized as the world’s premier jurisdiction for high-grade uranium deposits. These are the Pasfield Lake, Quark, and Nucleon projects.

    Pasfield Lake Project, Athabasca Basin

    The Pasfield Lake Project is Uranium One’s flagship Canadian uranium exploration asset, encompassing approximately 4,400 hectares in Saskatchewan’s eastern Athabasca Basin. Strategically located approximately 60 kilometres northwest of Cameco’s Cigar Lake Mine, the project occupies a highly prospective geological setting where favourable basement rocks, major regional fault systems, and historical exploration results combine to create an exceptional exploration opportunity.

    Click Image To View Full Size

    Historical work completed by previous operators has generated an extensive technical database, including airborne geophysical surveys, Audio Magnetotelluric (AMT) surveys, gravity surveys, geochemistry, and diamond drilling. This comprehensive dataset provides Uranium One with a strong foundation to apply modern exploration techniques and advanced targeting methods in the search for a significant uranium discovery.

    Quark Uranium Claim Group – Athabasca Basin

    The Quark Project consists of a large, contiguous land package of approximately 28,746 hectares (71,030 acres), situated within the highly productive Western Wollaston Domain and Wollaston–Mudjatik Transition Zone—host to the majority of Canada’s past and present uranium mines.

    Click Image To View Full Size

    Positioned adjacent to and along trend with major industry operators including Orano Canada and Fission Uranium, Quark benefits from proximity to established infrastructure, proven mineralization corridors, and active exploration success.

    Nucleon Claim Group

    The Nucleon Uranium Project consists of seven exploration-stage mineral claims totaling approximately 23,424.90 hectares located in northern Saskatchewan, Canada, within the Athabasca Basin.

    The project is organized into four prospective exploration areas situated along key uranium discovery corridors in the Basin.

    The Athabasca Basin hosts some of the highest-grade uranium deposits in the world and accounts for a significant portion of global uranium supply, making it one of the most important uranium-producing regions internationally.

    The Nucleon claims are positioned within an active uranium exploration district surrounded by major discoveries and development projects, including those operated by:

    • NexGen Energy (Arrow deposit)

    • Fission Uranium (Patterson Lake South deposit)

    • Denison Mines

    • Cameco

    This strategic location places the project within a highly prospective geological corridor known for multiple major uranium discoveries.

    Mineralization on nearby properties or at nearby mines is not necessarily indicative of mineralization on Uranium One’s properties.

    Click Image To View Full Size

    Qualified Person

    The scientific and technical information contained in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Lawrence Segerstrom, a consulting geologist who is a “Qualified Person” as such term is defined under National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects (“NI 43-101”).

    The QP reviewed the technical content, including the figures, historical data summaries, and adjacent property information, and confirms that the data have been accurately summarized where used.

The RSUs have a term of one year from the date of grant and are subject to the terms and conditions of the RSU Plan and applicable policies of the Canadian Securities Exchange (the “CSE”).

The Company is advancing a diversified portfolio of high-potential projects in Canada, Paraguay and Argentina, with a strategic focus on assets positioned to benefit from the increasing global demand for nuclear energy and secure energy supply chains.

data.title: Morocco expects stable fiscal deficit despite tax cuts in 2027
data.description:
By Ahmed Eljechtimi

Morocco expects a steady fiscal deficit at 3% of GDP despite higher spending on social programmes and tax cuts, newly appointed finance and economy minister Fouzi Lekjaa said on Friday.

The economy is expected to grow 3.7% in 2027, down from a forecast of 4.7% this year, assuming an average crop year, Lekjaa told members of parliament while presenting the 2027 draft budget.

Morocco announced a new government coalition last week following September 23 elections, placing priority on purchasing power, social services and youth employment, one year after GenZ protests and the Ceuta migration crisis in July.

The government's social policies in previous years have been weakened by an economic model that prioritised market forces over regulation, fostering monopolistic practices, rent-seeking and quick profits, Lekjaa said.

"Savage capitalism and neo-liberalism" have been at the heart of social tension, he said, urging a stronger role for the state in combating corruption, conflicts of interest and monopolies, while safeguarding food and energy sovereignty.

In total, the government plans to spend 62 billion dirhams ($6.3 billion) next year on measures aimed at improving social services, boosting purchasing power and reducing inequalities, Lekjaa said.

The measures include reforming distribution channels for basic goods, promoting youth employment and exempting salaries of less than 10,000 dirhams a month, which would account for 87% of all employees, from income tax, he said.

The package also includes pension increases, higher financial aid for needy families and electricity subsidies.

The health budget would rise 7% to 45.5 billion dirhams, while education spending would increase 4.6% to 121 billion dirhams, according to the draft budget.

The draft also authorises defence expenditure commitments of up to 190.5 billion dirhams.

Public debt is forecast to decline to 66.9% of GDP in 2027 from 67.5% this year, the budget document showed.

The government proposes raising to 40% the tax rate on profits above 100 million dirhams earned by fuel distribution companies, a sector previously sanctioned by competition authorities for anti-competitive practices.

The draft budget increases excise taxes on soft drinks, alcoholic beverages, cigarettes and e-cigarettes.

The government's financing requirement is expected to fall 7.4% to 159 billion dirhams in 2027 as it seeks to balance domestic and external borrowing "depending on market conditions," according to the draft budget.

data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Shares of Melar Acquisition Corp. I surged post market after the company noted in a Securities and Exchange filing that shareholders had approved a proposed business combination with Everli Global.

The stock climbed 73% to $19.00 after the closing bell. The stock closed down 3.2% at $11.00, and had risen 3.5% this year.

The deal for the special purpose acquisition company to take Everli public was approved at a Thursday shareholder meeting. The company announced the result on Thursday after the market closed.

data.title: France spared Moody's ratings downgrade as it struggles with unrest
data.description:
Key points:
  • Moody's leaves France rating at Aa3 with a negative outlook
  • S&P and Fitch have already cut France

By Leigh Thomas and Dhara Ranasinghe

Moody's spared France a credit rating downgrade on Friday, easing pressure on a government struggling to contain social unrest and shore up its strained finances.

Moody's said it had concluded a periodic review of its rating, leaving it at Aa3, which has carried a negative outlook since last October.

Bond markets had been pricing in a downgrade, which would have brought Moody's in line with Standard & Poor's and Fitch, which moved earlier as France struggled to rein in its public finances after a 2024 snap election produced a hung parliament and political paralysis.

The French finance ministry said in a statement that the fact Moody's kept its rating unchanged reflected the "credibility of the budget the government has put forward in the 2027 finance bill, which is designed to keep our public finances on the path to recovery."

The government is struggling to pass the bill in parliament, where opposition parties could refuse to compromise, reject the legislation and topple the government in a no-confidence vote.

"The Aa3 rating assumes that a deficit-reducing budget for 2027 will be adopted, while financing costs and social tensions will abate somewhat in the next few months," Moody's said in a statement.

French borrowing costs already exceed those of lower-rated peers such as Italy, as investors fret over the budget deficit — one of the euro zone's biggest — and a presidential election on April 18 and May 2 next year that polls suggest the far right could win.

TV images of weekend protests descending into riots and looting underscore the political difficulty of pushing budget cuts through.

That helped push the risk premium on French government debt over safe-haven German bonds to its highest in 15 years on Thursday, while France's benchmark 10-year bond yield hit 5.14%, its highest level since July 2002.

OUTLOOK IN FOCUS

Moody's said earlier this month that the French government's ability to overcome "fragmentation in parliament" would be the key factor for its next rating move.

That task looks harder after violent protests over underfunded schools escalated last weekend into riots during mass cost-of-living demonstrations. The government has refused to release more school funding or raise the minimum wage, and further protests are planned for Saturday.

In parliament, the lower house has scrapped some key savings measures in the 2027 budget, which targets a deficit of 5% of output versus 5.4% this year. Opposition parties show little appetite for compromise before the election, scrapping some proposed cuts while adding spending.

"You want to wait and see how the narrative evolves over the next six months into the election. That's going to have a more meaningful impact on the spread," said Rushabh Amin, a portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments.

Pressure on French debt could grow after the presidential vote if Moody's, S&P and Fitch all cut France to BBB — just above junk status — potentially forcing sales by those investors with rating limits, said Mike Bell, head of market strategy at RBC BlueBay Asset Management.

"That's where it could really start to get more ugly," he added.

data.title: Elme Communities Announces Suspended NYSE Trading; Anticipates Trading Will Begin OTC Effective October 26, 2026
data.description:
BETHESDA, Md., Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Elme Communities (“Elme” or the “Company”) today announced that the New York Stock Exchange (“NYSE”) has exercised its discretionary authority in accordance with Section 802.01D of the NYSE Listed Company Manual to commence proceedings to delist Elme’s common shares of beneficial interest (the “Common Shares”) from the NYSE due to “abnormally low selling price” levels. The NYSE also immediately suspended trading of the Common Shares. Given the Company’s previously adopted Plan of Sale and Liquidation (as defined below), Elme does not intend to appeal the NYSE’s determination, and, therefore, it is expected that the Common Shares will be delisted.

The Company anticipates the Common Shares will commence trading over-the-counter (“OTC”) on Monday, October 26, 2026 under the symbol “ELMES”. There can be no assurance regarding the development or maintenance of an active OTC trading market or the liquidity of any such market. Investors are cautioned that trading securities OTC is more limited and subject to different restrictions than trading securities listed on a national securities exchange and are advised to consult their own brokers or advisors.

Anticipated Timing of Establishment of a Liquidating Trust and Company Dissolution

As previously disclosed, in accordance with the Plan of Sale and Liquidation approved by the Board of Trustees (the “Board”) on July 30, 2025 and by the shareholders of the Company on October 30, 2025 (the “Plan of Sale and Liquidation”), it is the Company’s continued intention to terminate its existence by voluntary dissolution effective November 6, 2026 (the “Effective Time”), which will occur following the NYSE’s delisting of our Common Shares. In addition, as previously disclosed, the Company expects that its share transfer books will close at the close of business (Eastern Time) on November 5, 2026.

Prior to the Effective Time, the Company intends to transfer all of its remaining assets and liabilities to a Maryland liquidating trust (the “Liquidating Trust”). The purpose of the Liquidating Trust will be to liquidate the remaining assets (which are expected to consist primarily of the net cash proceeds from property sales) of the Liquidating Trust and distribute the amounts remaining in the Liquidating Trust, if any, after satisfaction of all remaining liabilities (including any additional liabilities, costs and expenses that may arise during the wind-down process) to the holders of the beneficial interests of the Liquidating Trust (the “Beneficial Interests”) upon completion of the wind-down process and in connection with termination of the Liquidating Trust. All of the Beneficial Interests will be held by the shareholders of the Company, with each shareholder of the Company being deemed automatically to have received and hold a percentage of Beneficial Interests in the Liquidating Trust corresponding to such shareholder’s percentage ownership in the Company as of the close of business on the last day of trading of the Common Shares. Shareholders of the Company will not be required to take any action to receive Beneficial Interests in the Liquidating Trust. The actual amount and timing of payment of any additional liquidating distribution(s) from the Liquidating Trust will be determined by the trustee of the Liquidating Trust in their sole discretion. As previously disclosed, the Company expects FTI Consulting, Inc. to be retained to provide services in connection with completing the wind-down process, including the services of a liquidating trustee to serve as trustee of the Liquidating Trust.

Following the transfer of the Company’s assets and liabilities to the Liquidating Trust, subject to certain exceptions related to transfer by will, intestate succession or operation of law, Beneficial Interests in the Liquidating Trust will not be transferable, nor will holders of Beneficial Interests have authority or power to sell or in any other manner dispose of their Beneficial Interests. The Beneficial Interests will not trade on the NYSE, or any other exchange or OTC. Simultaneously, all of the outstanding Common Shares and certificates representing Common Shares will be automatically cancelled and will thereafter no longer be deemed outstanding. The rights of holders of Beneficial Interests will not be represented by any form of certificate or other instrument.

For a discussion of the tax consequences of the transfer of the Company’s assets to the Liquidating Trust and the deemed distribution of the Beneficial Interests to the shareholders, please see “Material U.S. Federal Income Tax Consequences - Tax Consequences of the Liquidating Trust” beginning on page 76 of the definitive proxy statement filed by the Company with the SEC on September 24, 2025 for the special meeting of shareholders held on October 30, 2025, which is available free of charge through the website maintained by the SEC at http://www.sec.gov or the Company’s website at www.elmecommunities.com. You are urged to consult your own tax advisor to determine the particular tax consequences to you of the transfer of the Company’s assets to the Liquidating Trust and the deemed distribution of Beneficial Interests to the shareholders, including the applicability and effect of any U.S. federal, state and local and foreign tax laws.

Based on guidance previously provided by the SEC in similar circumstances, assuming the Company terminates its existence as described above, the Company anticipates that the Liquidating Trust will be required to file only annual reports on Form 10-K (using the SEC file number of the Company) containing unaudited financial statements, as well as current reports on Form 8-K (also filed using the SEC file number of the Company).

About Elme Communities

Elme Communities is a Maryland real estate investment trust. Elme, in accordance with and as anticipated by the Plan of Sale and Liquidation, expects to dissolve on November 6, 2026. Prior to the Company’s dissolution, the Company intends to transfer all of its remaining assets to Elme Communities Liquidating Trust for the benefit of holders of the Common Shares in accordance with and as anticipated by the Plan of Sale and Liquidation.

data.title: Colt Silver Restates Spin-Out Tax Considerations for Shareholders, Engages Consultant and Issues Options
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - October 23, 2026) - Colt Silver Corp. ("Colt Silver") and Palamina Corp. ("Palamina") have received inquiries from shareholders regarding the potential tax consequences of the spin-out transaction involving the distribution of newly issued Palamina shares and Colt Silver shares. The following is an excerpt from page 43 of Palamina's Information Circular, outlining the anticipated Canadian tax consequences for shareholders resident in Canada:

The exchange of Palamina Shares for New Palamina Shares and Colt Shares pursuant to the Arrangement is intended to qualify as a tax-deferred reorganization of capital under Section 86 of the Tax Act. A Resident Holder who exchanges Palamina Shares for New Palamina Shares and Colt Shares pursuant to the Arrangement (the "Share Exchange") will be deemed to have received a taxable dividend equal to the amount, if any, by which the aggregate fair market value of the Colt Shares distributed to the Resident Holder pursuant to the Share Exchange at the time of the Share Exchange exceeds the "paid-up capital" (as defined in the Tax Act) ("PUC") of the Resident Holder's Palamina Shares determined at that time. Any such taxable dividend will be taxable as described below under "Holders Resident in Canada - Taxation of Dividends". However, the Corporation expects that the aggregate fair market value of all Colt Shares distributed pursuant to the Share Exchange under the Arrangement will not exceed the aggregate PUC of the Palamina Shares. Accordingly, the Corporation does not expect that any Resident Holder will be deemed to receive a taxable dividend on the Share Exchange.

Important Notice: This summary is provided for general informational purposes only, is not intended to constitute tax advice, and should not be relied upon as a substitute for independent professional advice. Shareholders are encouraged to consult their own tax advisors regarding the specific tax consequences of the arrangement in their individual circumstances. Shareholders should refer to Palamina's Information Circular for the complete discussion of the applicable tax considerations.

data.title: PHP Foundation 'under-funded' with one full-time staff member, director says
data.description:
Key points:
  • Funding comes from donations and grants
  • AI-related increase in coding has doubled foundation's workload
  • No evidence seen of vulnerabilities' pre-disclosure exploitation

By Toby Sterling

The discovery of two serious flaws in PHP this week set off a global scramble to keep websites safe from hackers, showing just how critical the three-decade-old open-source programming language is to the internet.

Yet the nonprofit foundation that supports PHP, which may underpin up to 70% of sites globally, operates on a shoestring budget.

“We have one full-time staff member (that's me) and 14 mostly part-time contractors,” Executive Director Elizabeth Barron of the PHP Foundation said via email in an interview on Friday. Board members are unpaid volunteers, and funding comes from donations and grants.

The foundation works with outside researchers and companies, including OpenAI and cybersecurity firms Wiz and Calif, to investigate security flaws and coordinate fixes, including Wednesday's patches.

While Web security company Cloudflare has reported millions of hacking attempts, Barron said the foundation had no evidence hackers were able to exploit the vulnerabilities before they were disclosed, or on sites that have been patched.

"We received no further indication from OpenAI, Wiz or Calif, with whom we're working closely on this issue, regarding any issues on patched systems,” she said.

Artificial intelligence has proved both a help and a burden to the foundation. It helped researchers find the flaws, which had been present for a decade, and Barron said it made programmers more efficient.

However, it is also increasing maintainers' workloads. The PHP project is receiving nearly twice as many proposed code changes as a year ago, “yet the number of contributors hasn't doubled,” she said. Reviewing contributions and bug reports requires “a massive amount of human input and experience.”

Recent events have shown how heavily companies and governments rely on PHP, Barron said.

“Given that reliance, it is clear that PHP is incredibly under-funded.”

data.title: Investors piled a record sum into a leveraged semiconductor ETF last week. Things didn't work out.
data.description:
By Christine Idzelis

They tried to buy the dip, but the dip kept dipping

Chip stocks have soared this year, but they've been under pressure in October.

Traders making bullish bets on chip stocks are getting walloped this month, as renewed fears have emerged about investment returns on the buildout of artificial intelligence.

The latest hiccup for the AI trade inspired investors to attempt to buy the dip last week. They poured a record sum into a risky leveraged exchange-traded fund designed to amplify daily returns on semiconductor shares.

The Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF SOXL, which aims to provide a return 300% of the daily swings of a popular underlying index, attracted a record $6.1 billion of inflows last week, according to FactSet data.

Unfortunately for them, semiconductor shares continued their slide this week, as the leveraged ETF fell another 10.8%, according to FactSet. That marked its third straight weekly decline. The ETF is on track to fall by more than 43% in October.

In other words, they tried to buy the dip, but the dip kept dipping.

Daily inflows into the leveraged ETF continued until Thursday - the day its shares took a huge dive as semiconductor stocks saw sharp selloff, FactSet data showed. Investors have been jittery about the AI trade, which has taken volatile daily swings this month so powerful as to make or break the S&P 500's performance on a given day.

"The semis have been so sensitive to the AI-infrastructure buildout," Mike Reynolds, vice president of investment strategy at wealth-management firm Glenmede, said in a phone interview Friday. "The AI trade has come under some skepticism here."

Shares of semiconductor companies have soared this year as their chips are needed for the development of AI, attracting a lot of investor attention. While huge demand for AI chips has powered their earnings growth, investors are watching companies' spending on their AI buildout carefully on concern that the aggressive pace may not be sustainable.

Big moves in semiconductor shares have created a frenzy around leveraged ETFs that use derivatives to juice up daily returns in the stock market. But using such ETFs as trading tools to speculate that stocks will climb can be extremely painful if they tumble instead.

Shares of the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF took a nasty fall on Thursday, with a 20.5% drop that marked its worst day since June 23, according to FactSet data. The loss wasn't as brutal for investors in the iShares Semiconductor ETF SOXX, which slumped 6.8%.

The Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF has seen a lot of red on a weekly basis so far this month, booking on Friday a third straight week of declines, according to FactSet data.

Investors are weighing chip stocks' valuations after their massive 2026 gains. The iShares Semiconductor ETF has skyrocketed almost 59% so far this year, even though semiconductor shares have come under pressure again lately.

"At these valuations and after a rally that's been this aggressive, it's healthy that investors are taking a sober second look" at the prospect for returns from this AI theme, said Reynolds. It's good that "investors are questioning this in real time before you reach those peak euphoria moments where things get completely detached from reality in fundamentals," he said.

The U.S. stock market fell Friday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, S&P 500 SPX and technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index COMP all closing lower. The S&P 500's information-technology sector XX:SP500.45 booked a third consecutive week of losses as chip stocks struggled, its longest weekly losing streak since March, according to FactSet data.

The iShares Semiconductor ETF was also down for a third straight week, on track for a monthly loss of 15.9%.

Chelsea Ng contributed

data.title: Nigeria Ebola case linked to virus found in Kenya index case, health minister says
data.description:
By Camillus Eboh and George Obulutsa

Genomic analysis of Nigeria's only confirmed Ebola case shows the virus is closely related to the strain detected in Kenya's index case, Nigeria's health minister Muhammad Ali Pate said on Friday, offering the first genetic link between the outbreaks.

Nigerian authorities said there is no evidence that the Kenya index case traveled to Nigeria or had a direct connection to the Nigerian case.

  • Pate said contacts linked to the case are being traced, quarantined and tested, with some results negative and others still pending

  • Nigeria has recorded only one confirmed Ebola case from a traveller who had visited Uganda

  • Uganda, which borders the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and has previously battled Ebola outbreaks, said on Friday it remained Ebola-free but was tightening precautions

  • Uganda's health ministry said traveller locator forms had been reinstated for all arrivals, regardless of country of origin

  • Uganda said travellers with a history of travel to the DRC, where the outbreak began, will not be permitted to transit the country

data.title: Stocks fall, but tech shares steady after selloff; oil hits highest in nearly six months
data.description:
Key points:
  • Wall Street stocks end lower
  • Oil prices extend recent gains
  • US Treasury yields up; France gets respite

By Caroline Valetkevitch and Marc Jones

Major stock indexes ended lower on Friday even as tech shares mostly steadied, while Brent crude oil rose to its highest level in nearly six months after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia.

The Nasdaq eased. European shares also ended lower.

An index of semiconductors rose 0.4%. On Thursday, it posted its biggest daily percentage drop since June after a report from Meta Platforms reignited worries about the AI trade. The S&P 500 technology index was also up 0.4%.

The S&P 500 energy sector rose 2.5%, hitting a record high. Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia fanned fears over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East, where United Arab Emirates authorities also reported an oil spill.

Brent crude futures settled at $116.72 a barrel, up $3.55 or 3.14%, their highest since April 29. US West Texas Intermediate crude closed at $103.27 a barrel, up $3.80 or 3.8%. Brent finished the week up 6% and WTI ended 2.3% higher.

US Treasury yields rose after the benchmark 10-year yield posted on Thursday its biggest one-day drop in nearly four years.

"There are still all these headwinds in terms of sticky inflation," said JoAnne Bianco, partner and senior investment strategist at BondBloxx Investment Management in Chicago.

The 10-year yield remained under 5% as concerns about the durability of a rally in AI-related stocks lingered. The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note was up 3.7 basis points at 4.99%.

AI SHARES MIXED

Investor focus remains on the earnings season, with robust corporate profit growth underpinning gains for major equity indexes this year.

Next week, about one-third of S&P 500 companies report quarterly results, including Alphabet , Microsoft and Amazon , three AI hyperscalers whose capital spending forecasts will be closely watched on Wall Street.

Meta shares ended down 1%, while Microsoft was up 0.7%. Shares of Alphabet and Amazon eased.

"After Meta's report, there's still anxiety over the AI trade to a certain extent," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth in Boston.

Investors also digested other corporate earnings news. American Express shares fell 3.7% after it reported results and its CEO said the company had good momentum, but needed to become a more "agile and efficient" organization.

Telecom company shares, including Verizon , dropped after a report that SpaceX was in talks with cellular infrastructure companies about launching a US wireless carrier program.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 652.82 points, or 1.23%, to 52,215.16; the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX lost 39.75 points, or 0.52%, to 7,623.68 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 53.52 points, or 0.21%, to 25,955.34.

For the week, the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq dropped 0.7%. The blue-chip Dow rose 0.4%, notching its third straight weekly gain.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe EURONEXT:IACWI fell 3.96 points, or 0.35%, to 1,118.97. Asia's bourses steadied overnight, with South Korea's KOSPI ending its session higher after shedding as much as 4% earlier.

EURO FALLS

The euro fell and was down for the week, while euro zone bonds stabilized after recent volatility.

The euro has been hit by concerns about unrest in France and the country's budget problems. France will deploy 70,000 police backed by specialist units for protests on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said.

The euro was last down 0.21% at $1.1191 .

European stocks recorded their steepest weekly loss since early September. The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.31% to close at 635.77 points. For the week, the benchmark is down about 1.4%.

French yields (FR10YT=RR), which were down 5 basis points at 5.04%, have risen nearly 27 bps this week, the most of any major euro zone country and the most in a week since late May.

A selloff in French government bonds this week pushed the country's debt risk premium to its highest level since the euro zone sovereign debt crisis in 2011.
